lineupSource: Yahoo Sport UK / Roundtable projected XI, 20 August 2026, cross-checked on 21 August against Fantasy Football Scout's Friday predicted line-ups and Chelsea's own report of Xabi Alonso's 20 August press conference, re-checked on 22 August against Goal's 21 August preview, the Evening Standard / Yahoo Chelsea XI piece of 20 August, Sports Mole's 21 August injury and suspension list and The Pride of London's predicted XI, and re-checked again on 23 August against Rotowire's 22 August predicted line-ups, Sports Illustrated's 23 August Chelsea predicted XI, Football365's 23 August match preview and Sky Sports' 23 August team-news page. Still a projection, not team news — Sky confirmed on 23 August that no official sheet exists for either side, and none will until roughly an hour before Monday's 20:00 BST kickoff.
lineupNote: Still a projection, and Friday's crop of previews widened the spread rather than narrowing it. This 3-4-2-1 remains the modal call — Yahoo Sport and Roundtable both keep Reece James in a back three with Pedro Neto and Marco Palestra as the wing-backs — but Goal's 21 August preview keeps the same back three and reads the front as a 3-4-3 — João Pedro flanked by Palmer and Morgan Rogers rather than playing off a lone striker — with Romeo Lavia in the midfield two ahead of Enzo Fernández; the Evening Standard goes to a 4-3-3 with Jorrel Hato at left-back and James at right-back; and The Pride of London keeps James at right wing-back and promotes Josh Acheampong into the back three alongside Colwill and Lacroix. Four previews, four different answers on the back three, which with the left wing-back slot remains the least settled call here. Wesley Fofana is suspended, a ban carried over from his final-day red card at Sunderland that pre-season friendlies do not clear, and that is what pushes James from midfield into the back three. How long that ban runs is genuinely unclear: it has been reported as a single match, but the Sunderland dismissal was his second two-yellow red of 2025-26 after the one against Burnley, and at least one outlet has him banned for Alonso's first two games — Fulham and Brighton. No mainstream preview commits to a length, and none of it changes Monday: he is out at Craven Cottage either way. Enzo Fernández is staying — Alonso said flatly that Enzo is a Chelsea player once Manchester City let Chelsea's 14 August bid deadline pass — and is expected to feature. Palestra, the £43m signing from Atalanta and Serie A Defender of the Year after 37 loan appearances at Cagliari, can play either flank, so the left wing-back call still turns on whether Alonso wants his attacking edge there ahead of Hato or of Pep Chavarría, the £16.3m arrival from Rayo Vallecano signed to replace Marc Cucurella. The absence list hardened since Thursday: Goal now lists Caleb Wiley, Jordan Henderson, Aaron Anselmino, Mamadou Sarr, Emanuel Emegha and Geovany Quenda as ruled out, though the Standard the same day still files Henderson (wrist) and Emegha (hamstring) as doubts rather than definite absentees. Alonso reported no fresh injury concerns and said Danny Welbeck, managed through a minor problem, returns to team training on Saturday and can be involved. The standing caveat is unchanged: James, Fernández, Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers all reported back late from the World Cup and are selectable but may be eased in, so any of the four could start on the bench.

lineupSource: Sports Mole's 26 August Chelsea v Luton Town EFL Cup preview, which supplies this exact 4-2-3-1 and is the only preview whose availability list matches Xabi Alonso's own Wednesday press conference. Cross-checked against Sports Illustrated's 26 August Chelsea predicted line-up and 101 Great Goals' preview, plus Chelsea's own match preview for kick-off and UK broadcast, the Sky Sports Carabao Cup 2026-27 fixture listing, and CBS Sports / Paramount+ for the US rights position. Still a projection, not team news — no official sheet exists until roughly an hour before Thursday's 19:30 BST kickoff.
lineupNote: A guess, and a lower-confidence one than usual: this is a rotation night, and rotation is the hardest thing to predict. Three previews produced three different shapes — Sports Mole a 4-2-3-1, Sports Illustrated a 3-4-2-1, 101 Great Goals a 4-3-3 — and only seven names appear in all three (Penders, Acheampong, Lacroix, Chavarría, Barco, Estêvão, Welbeck). Sports Mole's XI is used here because its availability list is the only one that squares with what Alonso actually said on Wednesday. Alonso has signalled wholesale changes, so first Chelsea starts are in play for Danny Welbeck, Valentín Barco, Pep Chavarría and goalkeeper Mike Penders, with Penders getting the kind of look that decides whether he pushes Robert Sánchez. Two source conflicts are worth stating plainly rather than smoothing over. First, Wesley Fofana: Sports Mole has him serving the second match of a two-game ban and therefore out tonight, while Sports Illustrated and 101 Great Goals both start him. The two-game reading is the better-supported one and is what this site has used for Sunday's Brighton page — a red-card ban runs across domestic competitions, so the opener plus this tie discharges it and he is clear for Brighton, not for Luton. He is left out here on that basis, but it is a genuine disagreement, not a settled fact. Second, 101 Great Goals starts Marco Palestra, which looks stale: Alonso ruled Palestra out on Wednesday alongside Moisés Caicedo, and was notably less hopeful about Palestra — “Both not for tomorrow. Hopefully Moi can make it for the weekend. Maybe we need to check a little bit more with Marco.” Cole Palmer is not injured; he is expected to be rested with Sunday in mind. Jordan Henderson (wrist) is out and targeting 6 September at Arsenal, Emanuel Emegha's status is reported inconsistently — Sports Mole has him fit and available, 101 Great Goals still lists a hamstring problem — and Aaron Anselmino (hamstring) is a doubt. Enzo Fernández is fit and expected to be involved in some capacity, though Manchester City interest and a 1 September window deadline make him the one selection Alonso may be managing for non-football reasons. Geovany Quenda's key stat is deliberately blank: he moved from Sporting CP this summer and the public 2025-26 numbers for him conflict badly across sources, so nothing is stated rather than guessed.
notes: Xabi Alonso's first competitive home match as Chelsea manager. Luton are a League One side managed by former Arsenal midfielder Jack Wilshere, and arrive having won the EFL Trophy last season. Alonso's Wednesday press conference ruled out Caicedo and Palestra for this tie. Expect heavy rotation. The third-round draw was made on Wednesday evening, before this tie is played: the winner goes away to Leeds United, in the weeks beginning 7 or 14 September.

Alonso's first home game in charge. The rescheduling question is settled: the Premier League's August-September fixture-amendment notice confirms this as Sunday 30 August, 14:00 BST, moved to accommodate Brighton's UEFA Conference League playoff tie the preceding Thursday. Chelsea also had an EFL Cup tie against Luton on Thursday 27 August, three days before this one, so rotation is a live factor. Brighton arrive short of forwards: Yankuba Minteh (leg) is out for several weeks, Evan Ferguson (ankle) is not expected back until late October or November, Stefanos Tzimas (knee) is targeted for early-to-mid October, and Kaoru Mitoma is still working back from summer hamstring surgery — Hürzeler says he is getting closer but he is not available here. Jack Hinshelwood picked up a training injury and Hürzeler called the weekend likely too soon for him. Georginio Rutter has been in a protective boot since the Aston Villa fixture and faces a late fitness test; he is the more likely of the two to feature but is now a genuine doubt rather than a probable. New signings Promise David and Jaouen Hadjam are expected to be options, and Pascal Struijk and Ferdi Kadioğlu are back in the squad. The practical read: Brighton are missing four of their forward options and may be without a fifth, so Chelsea's back three should face a less direct attacking threat than Brighton's league position suggests.
lineupSource: Last Word on Football confirmed lineups, published 6:20 AM CT; corroborated by The Chelsea Chronicle team-sheet report at 6:57 AM CT
lineupNote: Seven changes, and the projection could not have caught the biggest one: Chelsea announced the signing of Emiliano Martínez from Aston Villa for about £7.5m on Sunday morning and he went straight into goal. Robert Sánchez was left out of the squad entirely and Mike Penders dropped to the bench. Enzo Fernández was also omitted amid Manchester City interest. Alonso reverted to a back three after using 4-2-3-1 against Luton, with Fofana back from suspension alongside Lacroix and Colwill. Neto, Lavia and Hato all returned, Malo Gusto was pushed into midfield, and Reece James was rested. Substitutes: Penders, Acheampong, Chavarría, James, Barco, Caicedo, Estêvão, Gittens, Welbeck.

notes: Alonso's first competitive meeting with childhood friend Mikel Arteta as a fellow manager. Arsenal are the reigning champions. This is Chelsea's first match since the summer transfer window shut on Tuesday 1 September, and it closed with two departures that change the team. Enzo Fernandez has gone to Manchester City for GBP 125m on a five-year deal, a British-record-equalling fee and a reunion with Enzo Maresca; Chelsea booked roughly an GBP 18m profit on the fee they paid Benfica three and a half years ago. Chelsea had lined up Monaco's Lamine Camara as the replacement and that deal collapsed late on deadline day, so there is no direct like-for-like signing to slot in. Goalkeeper Robert Sanchez also left, joining Cesc Fabregas's Como on a season-long loan, which leaves Emiliano Martinez and Mike Penders as the senior keepers. Marc Guiu moved to RB Leipzig. Availability: Moises Caicedo is a genuine doubt after picking up a knock, with Alonso saying only 'hopefully it wasn't more than last time' and that the club would assess him during the week. Jordan Henderson is still out following wrist surgery and Alonso has no return date for him. Marco Palestra has yet to feature this season after a training injury. Arsenal's own team news is not out yet, as Arteta's pre-match press conference falls later in the week. Chelsea then host Leeds United in the Carabao Cup third round on the Wednesday, three days after this, so squad management is again in play.
lineupSource: Projection, not a team sheet. Built from the confirmed Chelsea XI for matchweek 2, the 2 September Chelsea availability report in the Evening Standard/Yahoo (Caicedo, Henderson, Palestra), and Sky Sports and ESPN confirmation of the Enzo Fernandez and Robert Sanchez departures on 1 September. Alonso's pre-match press conference had not taken place when this was written.
lineupNote: This is a guess. The starting point is that Alonso named this exact eleven in the back-three shape last time out and has no obvious reason to break it up, so the projection is an unchanged side. Deadline day narrows his options rather than widening them: with Enzo Fernandez sold to Manchester City and the Lamine Camara deal dead, the central pair is Gusto alongside Lavia, and Moises Caicedo is a doubt, so there is little cover in there. Martinez keeps the goalkeeping job by default now that Robert Sanchez is on loan at Como. Reece James, Valentin Barco, Josh Acheampong, Estevao, Jamie Gittens and Danny Welbeck are the likeliest bench options, and James is the most credible name to force his way in, either at right centre-back or in midfield. Treat everything here as provisional until the team sheet lands about an hour before kickoff.
